FCT-001.q: Foreign contractor tax (FCT) is the common name for:
o: The VAT and CIT (or PIT for individuals) payable by foreign organisations/individuals doing business or earning income in Vietnam
A separate tax with its own law
Special consumption tax on foreign services
FCT-001.e: FCT is not a separate tax but a mechanism to collect VAT and CIT/PIT from foreign contractors.
FCT-001.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC (remaining VAT provisions); Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC (CIT part); Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: 'Foreign contractor tax' is the mechanism for collecting VAT and CIT (or PIT for individuals) from foreign parties doing business or earning income in Vietnam under contracts – usually withheld by the Vietnamese party.
Distractors: B – there is no separate law; C – import duty is a different tax; D – excise is unrelated.

FCT-002.q: Select ALL payments to foreign parties that ARE subject to FCT:
o: Interest paid to a foreign bank
Royalties for production technology paid to a foreign company
Plant operations management consulting by foreign experts performed in Vietnam
Online training provided by a foreign company to staff in Vietnam
Pure import of machinery with no services performed in Vietnam
Hiring a foreign company to advertise products in overseas markets
FCT-002.e: Pure supply of goods without services in Vietnam and advertising/marketing abroad are outside FCT; online training is still subject to FCT.
FCT-002.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: In scope: (A) interest to a foreign bank; (B) technology royalties; (C) consulting performed in Vietnam; (D) online training for staff in Vietnam (consumed in Vietnam though delivered remotely).
Distractors: (E) Pure goods supply without services in Vietnam; (F) advertising and marketing abroad – excluded.

FCT-003.q: Select ALL cases NOT subject to FCT:
o: Services provided and consumed outside Vietnam
Repair of vehicles, machinery and equipment abroad
Supply of goods delivered at the border gate without services in Vietnam
Installation and commissioning of a production line at a factory in Vietnam
FCT-003.e: Installation and commissioning performed in Vietnam is subject to FCT.
FCT-003.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Out of scope: (A) services supplied and consumed abroad; (B) repairs of vehicles and machinery abroad; (C) investment and trade promotion abroad; (D) goods delivered at the border without services.
Distractors: (E) Installation and commissioning at a Vietnamese plant are services in Vietnam → subject to contractor tax (including bundled goods at 1%).

FCT-004.q: Match the foreign contractor's income type with the CIT rate on revenue:
p: Value of goods supplied with services in Vietnam
FCT-004.e: Common CIT percentages on revenue for contractors using the direct method.
FCT-004.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Common CIT deemed rates on revenue: interest 5%; royalties 10%; goods supplied with services in Vietnam 1%; construction and installation 2%. Also ordinary services 5%, transport 2%, securities transfers 0.1%.

FCT-005.q: Interest paid to a foreign credit institution is not subject to VAT, so the Vietnamese party withholds only contractor CIT.
FCT-005.e: True. Lending is a non-VAT financial service; contractor CIT on interest is 5%.
FCT-005.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15 (Article 5); Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Credit services aren't subject to VAT (VAT-011), so on interest paid abroad the Vietnamese party withholds only CIT at 5% (or a lower/zero treaty rate with proper documents).

FCT-006.q: Technology transfer and IP transfer fees under specialised laws are not subject to contractor VAT.
FCT-006.e: True. Technology and IP transfers are not subject to VAT but remain subject to contractor CIT (royalties 10%).
FCT-006.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15 (Article 5).
Analysis: True. Technology transfers and IP assignments under specialised law aren't subject to VAT (with the required contract/registration). CIT still applies at 10% on royalties.

FCT-007.q: A supply-chain management consulting contract with a foreign company (direct method) is priced at VND 420 million, inclusive of contractor tax borne by the foreign party. VAT percentage 5%. How much contractor VAT does the Vietnamese party withhold (VND)?
FCT-007.e: VAT taxable revenue = 420 million (tax-inclusive price). VAT = 420 × 5% = 21,000,000 VND.
FCT-007.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: A gross price → the VAT base is the full 420 million. VAT = 420 × 5% = 21,000,000 VND.
Note: Under the direct method, the VAT ratio applies to the taxable revenue (no division by 1 + rate).

FCT-008.q: A supply-chain consulting contract with a foreign company (direct method) is priced at VND 420 million, inclusive of contractor tax borne by the foreign party; VAT percentage 5%, CIT percentage 5%. How much contractor CIT must the Vietnamese party withhold (VND)?
FCT-008.e: CIT revenue excludes VAT: 420 − 21 = 399 million. CIT = 399 × 5% = 19,950,000 VND.
FCT-008.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: The CIT base excludes VAT: 420 − 21 (FCT-007) = 399 million. CIT = 399 × 5% = 19,950,000 VND.
Note: 420 × 5% = 21 million is wrong as contractor VAT wasn't removed from the CIT base.

FCT-009.q: A service contract with a foreign contractor has a net price of VND 180.5 million (Vietnamese party bears all taxes). CIT rate 5%, VAT rate 5%. What total contractor tax (VAT + CIT) does the Vietnamese party pay (VND)?
FCT-009.e: CIT revenue = 180.5 / (1 − 5%) = 190 million → CIT 9.5 million. VAT revenue = 190 / (1 − 5%) = 200 million → VAT 10 million. Total 19,500,000 VND.
FCT-009.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working (gross-up of a net price): CIT base = 180.5 / (1 − 5%) = 190 million → CIT 9.5 million. VAT base = 190 / (1 − 5%) = 200 million → VAT 10 million. Total 19.5 million VND.
Check: 200 − 10 − 9.5 = 180.5 = the contractor's net receipt.

FCT-010.q: Interest to a foreign bank under a net contract is VND 95 million (Vietnamese party bears tax); interest is not subject to VAT; CIT rate 5%. What is the contractor CIT (VND)?
FCT-010.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Interest is VAT-exempt; gross up for CIT: 95 / (1 − 5%) = 100 million; tax = 5,000,000 VND.
Note: 95 × 5% = 4.75 million is wrong – a net price must be grossed up.

FCT-011.q: A company pays VND 200 million in royalties for warehouse-management software to a foreign company (tax-inclusive; software not subject to VAT); CIT rate 10%. What is the contractor CIT (VND)?
FCT-011.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: A gross price and software is VAT-exempt → CIT base = 200 million; tax = 20,000,000 VND.
Note: Check the treaty with the supplier's country – some set royalty rates below 10%.

FCT-012.q: A contract includes imported CNC machines worth VND 2 billion (import VAT paid) and installation/training services in Vietnam of VND 300 million (tax-inclusive, separately stated). Service VAT 5%; CIT: goods 1%, services 5%. What is the total contractor CIT (VND)?
FCT-012.e: Goods: 2,000 × 1% = 20 million. Services: VAT 300 × 5% = 15 million; CIT (300 − 15) × 5% = 14.25 million. Total CIT 34,250,000 VND.
FCT-012.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Goods (separately priced): CIT 2,000 × 1% = 20 million (VAT paid at import). Services: VAT = 300 × 5% = 15 million; CIT = (300 − 15) × 5% = 14.25 million. Total CIT = 34.25 million VND.
Note: If the contract doesn't split goods and services, the whole value takes the service rate – a worse outcome.

FCT-013.q: A Vietnamese party contracting with a foreign contractor using the direct method must withhold, declare and pay contractor tax before payment.
FCT-013.e: True. The Vietnamese party withholds and pays on behalf.
FCT-013.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. For direct-method contractors, the Vietnamese contracting party withholds, files and pays before payment – otherwise it bears the tax, interest and penalties (FCT-087).

FCT-014.q: VAT paid by the Vietnamese party on behalf of a foreign contractor (with tax payment receipts) is deductible input VAT if the Vietnamese party uses the credit method.
FCT-014.e: True. The tax payment receipt for VAT paid on behalf is the basis for deduction.
FCT-014.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15; Circular 69/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. The tax payment receipt for VAT paid on the foreign contractor's behalf supports the Vietnamese party's input VAT credit (credit method), in place of a VAT invoice – the contractor issues no Vietnamese invoice.

FCT-015.q: The three methods of paying contractor tax are:
o: Declaration method, direct (percentage-of-revenue) method and hybrid method
FCT-015.e: Hybrid method: VAT by credit, CIT as a percentage of revenue.
FCT-015.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Three methods: (1) declaration – the contractor registers, files credit-method VAT and CIT on actual profit; (2) direct – percentages of revenue, withheld by the Vietnamese party; (3) hybrid – credit-method VAT, CIT by percentage.
Distractors: B and C use non-existent labels; D omits the other two.

FCT-016.q: The filing deadline for per-transaction contractor tax withheld by the Vietnamese party is:
o: No later than the 10th day after the tax obligation arises
The last day of the following quarter
Together with the annual CIT finalisation
FCT-016.e: Per-transaction filing: no later than the 10th day from the day after the obligation arises (Decree 252/2026/ND-CP).
FCT-016.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Per-transaction filing is due by the 10th day after the tax point (usually the payment date). Monthly filing may be used for multiple payments in a month as regulated.
Distractors: B is the monthly deadline; C and D don't apply to per-transaction filing.

FCT-017.q: From 12/3/2026, contractor CIT rules follow Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC instead of the corresponding part of Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC.
FCT-017.e: True. Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC remains only partly in force.
FCT-017.x:
Basis: Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC; Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. From 12/03/2026, the CIT part of Circular 103/2014 is replaced by Circular 20/2026; contractor VAT and other Circular 103 content continue where not superseded.

FCT-018.q: Foreign suppliers of e-commerce and digital services without a PE in Vietnam may register, file and pay tax directly via the tax authority's portal for foreign suppliers.
FCT-018.e: True. This is the tax mechanism for cross-border business.
FCT-018.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Foreign e-commerce and digital service suppliers without a PE (online ads, content platforms, software…) may register, file and pay directly via the foreign supplier portal; Vietnamese buyers then needn't withhold.

FCT-019.q: To apply DTA exemptions/reductions, the most important document to collect from the foreign partner is:
o: A certificate of residence issued by the tax authority of the residence country
FCT-019.e: A certificate of residence (consularised as required) proves the partner is a resident of the treaty country.
FCT-019.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: A certificate of residence from the partner's tax authority (legalised as required) proves treaty residence – the precondition for treaty benefits.
Distractors: B, C and D don't prove tax residence.

FCT-020.q: A double taxation agreement can only reduce or exempt tax; it cannot increase tax above domestic law.
FCT-020.e: True. If the treaty rate is higher than domestic law, the domestic rate applies.
FCT-020.x:
Basis: Double taxation agreements; Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Treaties allocate taxing rights and cap source-country tax; they don't create new liabilities. If the treaty rate exceeds the domestic rate, the lower domestic rate applies.

FCT-021.q: Law 67/2025/QH15 adds business through e-commerce and digital platforms to the concept of a permanent establishment of foreign enterprises.
FCT-021.e: True. This is new to tax the cross-border digital economy.
FCT-021.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. The new law extends the permanent establishment concept to business conducted via e-commerce and digital platforms – adapting to the digital economy where foreign firms earn heavily in Vietnam without physical presence.

FCT-022.q: Two enterprises are related when one directly or indirectly holds at least what share of the other's capital?
FCT-022.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP (amended by Decree 20/2025/ND-CP).
Analysis: Ownership test: one party directly or indirectly holding at least 25% of the other's owner equity → related parties.
Distractors: 20% and 10% are below the threshold; 50% is the accounting control threshold, not the TP test.

FCT-023.q: Select ALL cases giving rise to a related-party relationship under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP:
o: Company A owns 30% of Company B
Two companies each more than 25% owned by the same individual
A loan from another enterprise of at least 25% of the borrower's equity and more than 50% of its medium/long-term debt
The two companies' general directors are spouses
A customer buys 20% of the company's output under an ordinary commercial contract
FCT-023.e: Ordinary commercial relationships do not create related parties; ownership, control, financing and family ties of managers do.
FCT-023.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; Decree 20/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Related: (A) 30% ownership (≥ 25%); (B) one individual holds over 25% of both; (C) a loan ≥ 25% of the borrower's equity and > 50% of its medium/long-term debt; (D) chief executives are spouses (family relationship).
Distractors: (E) A customer buying 20% of output under ordinary commercial terms isn't a related-party criterion.

FCT-024.q: Decree 20/2025/ND-CP amends the financing/guarantee criterion: loans from credit institutions that do not participate in management, control or capital of the borrower do not create a related-party relationship.
FCT-024.e: True. This avoids treating companies with large bank loans as related to the bank.
FCT-024.x:
Basis: Decree 20/2025/ND-CP amending Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Previously, heavy bank borrowing could make a company 'related' to its bank. Decree 20/2025 excludes loans from credit institutions that don't participate in management, control or equity – focusing on genuine control.

FCT-025.q: Total deductible interest for an enterprise with related-party transactions must not exceed:
o: 30% of net operating profit plus interest expense (net of deposit and lending interest) plus depreciation
FCT-025.e: The 30% EBITDA cap under Article 16(3) of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
FCT-025.x:
Basis: Article 16(3) of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Net interest (after deposit and lending interest) is deductible up to 30% of (net operating profit + net interest + depreciation) – i.e., 30% of EBITDA as defined by the Decree.
Distractors: B, C and D use the wrong base.

FCT-026.q: An enterprise with related-party transactions: net operating profit VND 20 billion; net interest expense (after deposit interest) 15 billion; depreciation 10 billion. How much interest is NOT deductible this year (VND)?
FCT-026.e: EBITDA = 20 + 15 + 10 = 45 billion; cap 30% × 45 = 13.5 billion; non-deductible 15 − 13.5 = 1.5 billion = 1,500,000,000 VND (carried forward).
FCT-026.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; Decree 20/2025/ND-CP.
Working: EBITDA = 20 + 15 + 10 = 45 billion. Cap = 30% × 45 = 13.5 billion. Net interest 15 → 1.5 billion non-deductible, carried forward (up to 5 years).

FCT-027.q: Interest disallowed because it exceeds the 30% cap may be carried forward to subsequent tax periods for up to 5 consecutive years.
FCT-027.e: True, provided total deductible interest in later periods still does not exceed 30%.
FCT-027.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; Decree 20/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Excess interest carries forward for up to 5 consecutive years and is deductible only if total deductible interest of the later year (including the carried amount) stays within 30% of that year's EBITDA.

FCT-028.q: The 30% cap applies to the total interest expense of an enterprise with related-party transactions, not only interest from related parties.
FCT-028.e: True. The cap applies to total interest (excluding prescribed items such as ODA and Government concessional loans).
FCT-028.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; Decree 20/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Once a company has related-party transactions, the 30% cap applies to its total net interest (including independent bank loans), not just related-party interest; only specific loans like ODA and Government concessional loans are excluded (FCT-093).

FCT-029.q: An enterprise is exempt from preparing transfer pricing documentation when:
o: Total revenue is below VND 50 billion and total related-party transactions are below VND 30 billion in the tax period
Total revenue is below VND 200 billion
It only transacts with its parent
FCT-029.e: Exemptions also apply with an APA or for simple-function entities meeting minimum margins.
FCT-029.x:
Basis: Article 19 of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: TP documentation is exempt when revenue < 50 billion and related-party transactions < 30 billion in the year. Other exemptions: an APA; simple functions with revenue < 200 billion meeting minimum margins (FCT-030).
Distractors: B is only one condition of the simple-function case; C and D aren't exemption grounds.

FCT-030.q: Simple-function enterprises with revenue below VND 200 billion are exempt from TP documentation if their EBIT margin on revenue is at least:
FCT-030.x:
Basis: Article 19(2) of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Simple-function companies with revenue < 200 billion and no intangible transactions are exempt if EBIT/revenue reaches at least: distribution 5%; manufacturing 10%; toll processing 15%.

FCT-031.q: The standard arm's length range for comparison under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP is:
o: The full range of comparable data
FCT-031.e: If the taxpayer's result is below the 35th percentile, it is adjusted to the median.
FCT-031.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: The arm's length range is the 35th to 75th percentile of comparables (narrower than OECD's 25–75 interquartile range). Results outside it are adjusted to the median.
Distractors: B is OECD practice; C and D are too wide.

FCT-032.q: When an enterprise's margin is below the 35th percentile of the arm's length range, the tax authority adjusts it to the median.
FCT-032.e: True. The median is the 50th percentile.
FCT-032.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. If the company's margin is below the 35th percentile, the authority adjusts to the median (50th) – not to the 35th – so adjustments can be large (FCT-078).

FCT-033.q: Match each transfer pricing method with its international name:
FCT-033.e: The five methods in Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, consistent with OECD guidance.
FCT-033.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.
Analysis: Five methods: comparable uncontrolled price (CUP); Resale Price; Cost Plus; Transactional Net Margin (TNMM); Profit Split. Selection depends on functional analysis (functions, assets, risks) and data availability.

FCT-034.q: Select ALL components of transfer pricing documentation:
FCT-034.e: TP documentation has three tiers: Local file, Master file, CbCR.
FCT-034.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; BEPS Action 13.
Analysis: Three-tier documentation: (A) Local file; (B) Master file; (C) CbCR where required.
Distractors: (D) Internal audit reports and (E) AGM minutes aren't part of TP documentation.

FCT-035.q: A Vietnamese ultimate parent must prepare a CbCR when global consolidated revenue in the tax period is at least:
FCT-035.e: The CbCR threshold under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP is VND 18,000 billion.
FCT-035.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: An ultimate parent in Vietnam with global consolidated revenue of 18,000 billion VND or more must prepare a CbCR (roughly the OECD EUR 750 million threshold).
Distractors: B and D are lower; C uses the wrong unit and amount for Vietnam.

FCT-036.q: During an audit or inspection, the enterprise must provide TP documentation within:
FCT-036.e: 15 working days (one extension allowed for valid reasons).
FCT-036.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: During audits, TP documentation must be provided within 15 working days of the request (one extension of up to 15 days with good reason).
Distractors: 5, 30 and 60 days are wrong.

FCT-037.q: TP documentation must be prepared and kept before filing the annual CIT finalisation.
FCT-037.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. TP documentation is contemporaneous – prepared and kept before filing the CIT return, reflecting data and pricing at the time; it can't be prepared retroactively at audit.

FCT-038.q: An enterprise transacting only with related parties that pay CIT in Vietnam, at the same rate, with no party enjoying incentives in the period, is exempt from TP declarations and documentation but must declare related-party information.
FCT-038.x:
Basis: Article 19(1) of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. When all related parties pay CIT in Vietnam at the same rate with no incentives, profit-shifting risk is low; the company is exempt from pricing declarations and documentation but still discloses related-party information.

FCT-039.q: A taxpayer's self-adjustment of related-party prices to the arm's length principle must not reduce tax payable.
FCT-039.e: True. Adjustments may only be made in the direction that does not reduce tax obligations.
FCT-039.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. One-way rule: self-adjustments to arm's length may only avoid reducing tax – i.e., they can only increase taxable income.

FCT-040.q: Decree 291/2026/ND-CP adds penalties for failing to provide information for international tax information exchange, including the CbCR.
FCT-040.e: True. Decree 291/2026/ND-CP adds Article 19a to Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
FCT-040.x:
Basis: Decree 291/2026/ND-CP amending Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Decree 291/2026 adds Article 19a to Decree 125/2020, penalising failure to provide (or incorrect) information for international tax exchange, including CbCR – meeting Vietnam's BEPS commitments.

FCT-041.q: An enterprise with an advance pricing agreement (APA) is exempt from TP documentation for transactions covered by the APA.
FCT-041.e: True. It submits APA annual reports instead.
FCT-041.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15 (APA).
Analysis: True. An APA agrees the pricing method with the tax authority in advance; transactions it covers are exempt from TP documentation, replaced by an annual APA report.

FCT-042.q: The global minimum effective tax rate under the GloBE rules is:
FCT-042.e: The global minimum rate is 15%; the shortfall is the top-up rate.
FCT-042.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: GloBE (Pillar Two) sets a 15% minimum effective rate per jurisdiction; any shortfall is the top-up rate.
Distractors: 10%, 20% and 12.5% aren't the GloBE standard (12.5% is Ireland's headline rate).

FCT-043.q: Top-up CIT under Resolution 107/2023/QH15 applies to constituent entities of MNE groups with consolidated revenue of:
o: EUR 750 million or more in at least 2 of the 4 preceding fiscal years
USD 750 million in the current year
VND 18,000 billion in the preceding year
FCT-043.e: Consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million in at least 2 of the 4 preceding fiscal years.
FCT-043.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Applies to constituent entities of MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million in at least 2 of the 4 preceding years.
Distractors: B uses USD and the current year; C is the CbCR threshold; D is too low.

FCT-044.q: Match each rule with its content under Resolution 107/2023/QH15:
p: Qualified domestic minimum top-up tax paid by the Vietnamese constituent entity
Income inclusion rule; a Vietnamese parent pays on low-taxed foreign income
Undertaxed profits rule, not yet applied by Resolution 107/2023/QH15
FCT-044.e: Vietnam applies the QDMTT and IIR from fiscal year 2024.
FCT-044.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: QDMTT – the qualified domestic minimum top-up tax paid by Vietnamese constituent entities. IIR – a Vietnamese parent pays top-up tax on low-taxed foreign subsidiaries. UTPR – the undertaxed profits rule, not yet applied by Resolution 107/2023.

FCT-045.q: Top-up CIT under Resolution 107/2023/QH15 applies from fiscal year 2024.
FCT-045.e: True. Decree 236/2025/ND-CP provides details and also applies from fiscal year 2024.
FCT-045.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The rules apply from FY2024; Decree 236/2025, though issued later, also covers FY2024, with an 18-month first-year deadline (FCT-048) giving time to prepare.

FCT-046.q: A group's effective tax rate in Vietnam is 10%; excess profit (after substance-based income exclusion) is VND 1,000 billion. What is the domestic top-up tax (simplified, no other adjustments) (VND)?
FCT-046.e: Top-up rate = 15% − 10% = 5%; top-up tax = 5% × 1,000 billion = 50 billion = 50,000,000,000 VND.
FCT-046.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Top-up rate = 15% − 10% = 5%. Top-up tax = 5% × excess profit 1,000 billion = 50 billion VND.
Note: Excess profit = net GloBE income − SBIE (FCT-050).

FCT-047.q: Select ALL entities excluded from the global minimum tax:
o: A manufacturing subsidiary with EUR 100 million revenue in an in-scope group
FCT-047.e: Ordinary operating subsidiaries of in-scope groups are within the scope.
FCT-047.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Excluded entities: (A) governmental entities; (B) international organisations; (C) non-profits; (D) pension funds (and certain investment funds and real estate vehicles as ultimate parents).
Distractors: (E) An ordinary operating subsidiary of an in-scope group is covered regardless of its own size.

FCT-048.q: The filing and payment deadline for the QDMTT for the first year in scope is:
o: The last day of the 18th month after fiscal year-end
FCT-048.e: First year: 18th month; subsequent years: 12th month after fiscal year-end.
FCT-048.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: First in-scope year: QDMTT return and payment by the last day of the 18th month after year-end; later years: the 12th month. The long deadline reflects reliance on group consolidated data.

FCT-049.q: Under the de minimis exclusion, a group may elect no top-up tax in a jurisdiction where average GloBE revenue is below EUR 10 million and average GloBE income below EUR 1 million.
FCT-049.e: True. This de minimis exclusion is domesticated by Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
FCT-049.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. De minimis: if average GloBE revenue is under EUR 10 million and average GloBE income under EUR 1 million in a jurisdiction, the group may elect zero top-up there – reducing compliance costs for small operations.

FCT-050.q: The substance-based income exclusion (SBIE) is based on:
o: Payroll costs of eligible employees and carrying value of eligible tangible assets
FCT-050.e: SBIE comprises a payroll carve-out and a tangible asset carve-out in the jurisdiction.
FCT-050.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: SBIE has two parts: a percentage of eligible payroll and a percentage of eligible tangible assets in the jurisdiction – reflecting real activity and reducing profit subject to top-up.
Distractors: B, C and D aren't GloBE substance factors.

FCT-051.q: QDMTT paid in Vietnam is credited when other countries apply the IIR to the same income, helping Vietnam retain taxing rights.
FCT-051.e: True. This is the main reason Vietnam enacted the QDMTT.
FCT-051.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Under GloBE, a qualified QDMTT is credited when the parent's country applies the IIR to the same income. Without a QDMTT, the parent's country would collect the top-up on Vietnamese profits.

FCT-052.q: A company pays VND 1,000 million in interest (tax-inclusive, borne by the foreign party) to a foreign bank; interest is not subject to VAT; CIT rate 5%. What is the contractor CIT (VND)?
FCT-052.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Gross price, interest VAT-exempt: 1,000,000,000 × 5% = 50,000,000 VND.
Note: If the lender is the parent (related), interest is also subject to the 30% EBITDA cap (FCT-025).

FCT-053.q: A contract sets a net software royalty of VND 90 million (Vietnamese party bears tax); not subject to VAT; CIT rate 10%. What is the contractor CIT (VND)?
FCT-053.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Net price, no VAT: gross up 90 / (1 − 10%) = 100 million; tax = 10,000,000 VND. Check: 100 − 10 = 90 = the contractor's receipt.

FCT-054.q: Select ALL obligations of an enterprise with related-party transactions under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP:
o: Declare related-party relationships and transactions with the CIT finalisation
Prepare and keep TP documentation (unless exempt)
Obtain tax authority permission before each related-party transaction
FCT-054.e: There is no pre-approval for each transaction; an enterprise may apply for an APA if it wishes.
FCT-054.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Obligations: (A) disclose related-party information with the return; (B) prepare and keep TP documentation (unless exempt); (C) apply the 30% EBITDA interest cap; (D) provide documentation on request.
Distractors: (E) No prior approval per transaction is required; an APA can be sought voluntarily.

FCT-055.q: An enterprise buying machinery from its foreign parent above arm's length prices may have prices adjusted and taxable income reassessed by the tax authority.
FCT-055.e: True. Comparability evidence against independent transactions is key.
FCT-055.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Buying machinery from the parent above arm's length inflates cost and depreciation and cuts Vietnamese profit; the authority may adjust prices and reassess taxable income. Comparable price (CUP) data or profit analysis are the defence.

FCT-056.q: Match each TP documentation component with its main content:
p: Group overview, value chain, transfer pricing policy
Information on the taxpayer, related-party transactions and comparability analysis
Allocation of income, taxes and activities of the group by country
FCT-056.e: Three-tier structure per OECD BEPS Action 13.
FCT-056.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; OECD BEPS Action 13.
Analysis: Master file – group overview, value chain, TP policies, intangibles. Local file – the taxpayer, specific related-party transactions, functional and comparability analysis. CbCR – revenue, profit, tax and headcount by country.

FCT-057.q: The QDMTT applies to Vietnamese constituent entities of in-scope groups even if the ultimate parent is in a country that has not applied the IIR.
FCT-057.e: True. The QDMTT ensures Vietnam collects top-up tax arising in Vietnam.
FCT-057.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. QDMTT applies to Vietnamese constituent entities of in-scope groups regardless of whether the parent's country applies the IIR – securing Vietnam's top-up on local profits.

FCT-058.q: The effective tax rate (ETR) under GloBE is:
o: Adjusted covered taxes / net GloBE income of the jurisdiction
Tax paid / global consolidated accounting profit
FCT-058.e: ETR is computed per jurisdiction (jurisdictional blending).
FCT-058.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
Analysis: GloBE ETR = covered taxes / net GloBE income, blended across all constituent entities in a jurisdiction.
Distractors: B uses revenue; C is the headline rate; D is global rather than per jurisdiction.

FCT-059.q: A group's adjusted covered taxes in Vietnam are VND 80 billion; net GloBE income is VND 1,000 billion. What is the top-up tax percentage (%)?
FCT-059.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15 (top-up tax under global anti-base-erosion rules); OECD GloBE Model Rules Art. 5.2.
Working: ETR = covered taxes / net GloBE income = 80 / 1,000 = 8%; top-up rate = 15% − 8% = 7%.
Analysis: Top-up tax = 7% × excess profit (net GloBE income − the substance-based carve-out: a percentage of payroll and tangible assets). With no carve-out: 7% × 1,000 = 70 billion – collected by Vietnam via its qualified domestic minimum top-up tax (QDMTT) rather than by the parent's country.

FCT-060.q: FDI enterprises of in-scope groups enjoying CIT incentives (preferential rates, exemptions, reductions) may have an ETR below 15% and incur top-up tax in Vietnam.
FCT-060.e: True. Hence investment incentives are shifting towards cost support (the Investment Support Fund).
FCT-060.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
Analysis: True. 10% rates and tax holidays lower covered taxes, pushing ETR below 15% → top-up tax that erodes the incentive. Policy is therefore shifting to cost support via the Investment Support Fund (R&D, training, infrastructure), which doesn't reduce ETR the same way.

FCT-061.q: A contract with a foreign expert for technical consulting in Vietnam has a net price of VND 95 million (Vietnamese party bears tax); VAT 5%, CIT 5%. What is the contractor VAT (VND million)?
FCT-061.e: CIT revenue = 95/0.95 = 100; VAT revenue = 100/0.95 = 105.263; VAT = 105.263 × 5% ≈ 5.263 million VND.
FCT-061.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Gross-up: CIT base = 95 / 0.95 = 100 million; VAT base = 100 / 0.95 ≈ 105.263 million; VAT ≈ 5.263 million (CIT = 5 million).
Check: 105.263 − 5.263 − 5 = 95 = the net price.

FCT-062.q: A turnkey construction and installation contract with a foreign contractor is priced at VND 5,000 million excluding VAT; CIT rate 2%. What is the contractor CIT (VND million)?
FCT-062.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: The VAT-exclusive price is the CIT base: 5,000 × 2% = 100 million VND.
Note: Check the rate depending on whether materials and equipment are included in the contract.

FCT-063.q: A Vietnamese company buys management software from a foreign supplier via a one-off payment for a time-limited licence. How is this payment taxed under FCT?
FCT-063.e: Software is not subject to VAT; payment for the right to use software is a royalty taxed at 10% CIT (unless a treaty provides otherwise).
o: No FCT because it is an intangible good
FCT-063.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Software is VAT-exempt (VAT-015); a payment for a time-limited software licence is a royalty, subject to 10% CIT (unless a treaty sets a lower rate or classifies it differently).
Distractors: B wrongly applies VAT; C is wrong as intangibles are in scope; D omits CIT.

FCT-064.q: Bank guarantee fees paid to a foreign bank are financial services taxed at contractor CIT like loan interest (5%).
FCT-064.e: True. Guarantee and commitment fees of an interest nature usually take 5% CIT; for VAT, credit services (including guarantees) are non-taxable.
FCT-064.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. Guarantee and commitment fees paid to foreign banks are interest-like, so CIT is 5%; for VAT, guarantees are credit services and non-taxable.

FCT-065.q: Arrange the steps for handling FCT when paying a foreign contractor (direct method):
FCT-065.e: Scope → taxable revenue → rates → withhold and pay → payment and record-keeping.
o: Determine whether the contract is subject to FCT
Determine gross/net price and taxable revenue
Apply VAT and CIT percentages by activity (considering treaties)
File and pay on behalf by the deadline
Pay the contractor and keep tax receipts
FCT-065.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) Confirm scope → (2) determine gross/net and the tax base (gross up if net) → (3) apply VAT and CIT rates; consider treaties → (4) file and pay within 10 days → (5) pay and keep tax receipts (for VAT credit and CIT deduction).

FCT-066.q: Under model double tax agreements (OECD/UN), business profits of a foreign enterprise are taxable in Vietnam only when:
FCT-066.e: Article 7 principle: the source country taxes only profits attributable to a PE; treaty application procedures apply.
o: It has a permanent establishment in Vietnam and the profits are attributable to that PE
The contract is signed in Vietnam
FCT-066.x:
Basis: Article 7 of the OECD/UN Model; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: A foreign enterprise's business profits are taxable in the source country (Vietnam) only if it has a PE there, and only on profits attributable to it. Benefits require a treaty notification (FCT-070).
Distractors: B, C and D aren't criteria for allocating taxing rights.

FCT-067.q: A foreign contractor using the hybrid method declares and credits VAT and pays CIT as a percentage of revenue.
FCT-067.e: True. Hybrid: VAT by the credit method, CIT as a percentage of revenue.
FCT-067.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Hybrid method: the contractor registers and files credit-method VAT like a domestic company, while CIT is paid as a percentage of revenue – for contractors whose books suffice for VAT but not for actual profit.

FCT-068.q: A net interest payment of VND 190 million is made to the foreign parent (Vietnamese party bears tax); interest is not subject to VAT; CIT rate 5%. What total interest cost (including tax paid on behalf) does the company record (VND million)?
FCT-068.e: Taxable revenue = 190/0.95 = 200; CIT paid on behalf 10; total cost = 200 million VND.
FCT-068.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Gross-up = 190 / 0.95 = 200 million; CIT paid on behalf = 10 million. Total interest expense = 190 + 10 = 200 million VND.
Note: All 200 million counts towards the 30% EBITDA cap since the lender is the parent.

FCT-069.q: FCT paid by the Vietnamese party under a net-price contract is deductible for the Vietnamese party's CIT.
FCT-069.e: True. When the contract has the Vietnamese party bear tax, the tax paid on behalf is part of the service price and deductible with proper documents.
FCT-069.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Under net contracts, contractor tax paid by the Vietnamese party is part of the service cost (gross price) and deductible with the contract and tax receipts. VAT paid on behalf is credited as input (FCT-014), not expensed.

FCT-070.q: Select ALL documents needed to apply treaty exemptions/reductions for a foreign contractor:
FCT-070.e: The treaty notification includes the prescribed form, certificate of residence, contract and power of attorney if any.
o: Certificate of residence from the residence country (prior year or as prescribed)
Copy of the contract with the Vietnamese party
Power of attorney (if a representative files)
FCT-070.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The treaty notification file: the prescribed notice; (A) certificate of residence; (B) contract copy; (C) power of attorney if filed by a representative.
Distractors: (D) The contractor's audited FS isn't required.

FCT-071.q: The current regulation on tax administration for enterprises with related-party transactions is:
FCT-071.e: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP (replacing Decree 20/2017) as amended by Decree 20/2025/ND-CP.
FCT-071.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; Decree 20/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The current TP rules are Decree 132/2020 (replacing Decree 20/2017), amended by Decree 20/2025.
Distractors: Decree 20/2017 is repealed; Circular 66/2010 is outdated; Decree 125/2020 covers tax penalties.

FCT-072.q: An enterprise with related-party transactions: net operating profit VND 8 billion; interest expense 6 billion; deposit interest income 1 billion; depreciation 7 billion. How much net interest is deductible for CIT this year (VND billion)?
FCT-072.e: Net interest = 6 − 1 = 5; EBITDA = 8 + 5 + 7 = 20; cap 30% × 20 = 6 billion ≥ 5, so all 5 billion is deductible.
FCT-072.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Working: Net interest = 6 − 1 = 5 billion. EBITDA = 8 + 5 + 7 = 20; cap = 6 billion ≥ 5 → all 5 billion deductible.
Note: The 1 billion headroom can absorb disallowed interest carried forward from prior years (if any).

FCT-073.q: An enterprise with related-party transactions must declare related-party information (Appendix I of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP) with its CIT finalisation, even when exempt from TP documentation.
FCT-073.e: True. A documentation exemption does not exempt the declaration of related-party information.
FCT-073.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Exemption from TP documentation doesn't remove the duty to file Appendix I (related-party information) with the CIT return – the authority's risk-assessment input.

FCT-074.q: The most suitable TP method for a distributor buying from its parent and reselling to independent parties without changing the product is:
FCT-074.e: Resale price suits distributors without further processing; TNMM is also common where gross margin data are lacking.
FCT-074.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; OECD Guidelines.
Analysis: A distributor buying from a related party and reselling unchanged to independents fits the resale price method, comparing gross margins with independent distributors. TNMM is also common when gross margin data is lacking.
Distractors: B is for highly integrated transactions; C for processing and services; D – CUP for services doesn't fit.

FCT-075.q: The cost plus method is usually most suitable for:
FCT-075.e: Cost plus compares the gross mark-up on costs with independent entities of similar functions (toll/contract manufacturing, services).
o: Toll/contract manufacturers or service providers to related parties
FCT-075.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; OECD Guidelines.
Analysis: Cost Plus compares mark-ups on cost with independent entities performing similar functions – suited to toll processing, contract manufacturing and intra-group services, where cost measures value created.
Distractors: B uses resale price; C – unique intangibles usually use profit split; D – loans use interest comparisons.

FCT-076.q: Service fees paid to related parties (group management fees) are deductible only if the services are actually provided, beneficial and priced at arm's length.
FCT-076.e: True. Decree 132/2020/ND-CP disallows fees for non-beneficial, duplicated or shareholder services.
FCT-076.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Group management fees are deductible only if (1) services were actually provided, (2) they bring economic or commercial benefit, (3) pricing is at arm's length. Evidence: work reports, emails, minutes, cost allocation keys.

FCT-077.q: Select ALL payments to related parties that are NOT deductible under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP:
FCT-077.e: Shareholder, duplicated and non-beneficial services are disallowed; genuine, beneficial, arm's length services are deductible.
o: Shareholder services (benefiting the parent, e.g., group board meetings)
Services duplicating those performed in-house or bought from independent parties
Services with no identifiable commercial benefit
Accounting services actually provided, contracted and priced at arm's length
FCT-077.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Non-deductible: (A) shareholder activities serving the parent as owner; (B) duplicative services; (C) services without identifiable commercial benefit.
Distractors: (D) Genuine accounting services under contract at arm's length are deductible.

FCT-078.q: The arm's length range of net margin on revenue: 35th percentile 4%, median 6%, 75th percentile 8%. An enterprise has a 3% margin on revenue of VND 200 billion. By how much is profit adjusted upward (VND billion)?
FCT-078.e: 3% < 4% (35th percentile) → adjust to the median 6%: (6% − 3%) × 200 = 6 billion VND.
FCT-078.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Working: 3% < the 35th percentile (4%) → adjust to the 6% median. Upward adjustment = (6% − 3%) × 200 billion = 6 billion VND.
Note: Adjusting only to the 4% lower bound (2 billion) is a common trap.

FCT-079.q: An enterprise whose margin lies between the 35th and 75th percentiles of the arm's length range is not adjusted.
FCT-079.e: True. Results within the standard range are accepted as arm's length.
FCT-079.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Results within the 35th–75th percentile range are deemed arm's length and not adjusted.

FCT-080.q: The decree detailing Resolution 107/2023/QH15 on top-up CIT is:
FCT-080.e: Decree 236/2025/ND-CP details the global minimum tax, applying from fiscal year 2024.
FCT-080.x:
Basis: Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Decree 236/2025 details Resolution 107/2023 on the global minimum top-up tax.
Distractors: Decree 132/2020 – transfer pricing; Decree 320/2025 – general CIT; Circular 20/2026 – CIT guidance.

FCT-081.q: In Vietnam, constituent entities have net GloBE income of VND 2,000 billion, adjusted covered taxes of 160 billion and SBIE of 400 billion. What is the top-up tax (simplified) (VND billion)?
FCT-081.e: ETR = 160/2,000 = 8%; top-up rate 7%; excess profit = 2,000 − 400 = 1,600; top-up tax = 7% × 1,600 = 112 billion VND.
FCT-081.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Working: ETR = 160 / 2,000 = 8% → top-up 7%. Excess profit = 2,000 − 400 (SBIE) = 1,600 billion. Top-up tax = 7% × 1,600 = 112 billion VND.

FCT-082.q: The global minimum tax applies to all FDI enterprises in Vietnam regardless of group size.
FCT-082.e: False. It applies only to constituent entities of MNE groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more in at least 2 of the 4 preceding years.
FCT-082.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
Analysis: False. The global minimum tax applies only to constituent entities of MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million in 2 of the 4 preceding years; FDI firms in smaller groups are out of scope.

FCT-083.q: Countries, including Vietnam, enact a QDMTT mainly to:
FCT-083.e: A QDMTT lets the source country collect top-up tax first; the parent's IIR credits the QDMTT paid.
o: Keep the right to collect top-up tax arising domestically rather than letting the parent's country collect via the IIR
FCT-083.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
Analysis: A QDMTT lets the source country collect the top-up first; the parent country's IIR credits it. The aim is to keep taxing rights at home.
Distractors: B – the headline rate is unchanged; C and D are unrelated.

FCT-084.q: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC adds account 82112 to record top-up CIT expense under global minimum tax rules.
FCT-084.e: True. Account 82112 – Top-up CIT expense under global minimum tax rules.
FCT-084.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Account 82112 – top-up CIT expense under global minimum tax rules (a sub-account of 8211 current tax), keeping it separate from ordinary CIT (CIT-086).

FCT-085.q: Match each outbound payment with its usual FCT treatment:
FCT-085.e: Common percentages under FCT guidance; pure goods delivered at the border are outside FCT.
p: Machinery delivered at port without services
FCT-085.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Parent loan interest – no VAT; CIT 5%. Trademark royalties – IP licences VAT-exempt as regulated; CIT 10%. Consulting in Vietnam – VAT 5%, CIT 5%. Machinery delivered at port without services – out of scope.

FCT-086.q: A company pays trademark royalties to its parent in a treaty country with a 10% maximum royalty rate; gross payment VND 1,000 million; the company's 2026 revenue is 50,000 million. How much contractor CIT is withheld (VND million)?
FCT-086.e: Domestic rate 10%, treaty not higher → 1,000 × 10% = 100 million VND. Annual revenue is irrelevant.
FCT-086.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; tax treaty.
Working: The domestic 10% doesn't exceed the 10% treaty cap → 10%: 1,000 × 10% = 100 million VND. Company revenue is a distractor.
Note: Royalties to the parent are also reviewed under TP rules for reasonableness.

FCT-087.q: An enterprise that fails to withhold FCT when paying a foreign contractor must still pay the tax in full and may face penalties and late-payment interest.
FCT-087.e: True. The Vietnamese party must withhold and pay; failure makes it liable for the tax, late interest and penalties under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
FCT-087.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The Vietnamese party must withhold; if it fails, it still pays the full tax (often grossed up if the contractor was paid in full), plus 0.03%/day interest and penalties for under-declaration under Decree 125/2020.

FCT-088.q: An FDI enterprise pays its parent management fees of 3% of revenue without reports or evidence of services. The main tax risk is:
FCT-088.e: A contract alone is insufficient; without benefit evidence the fee is disallowed; FCT obligations on payment still arise.
o: The cost is disallowed for CIT under TP rules, while FCT withheld still has to be paid
No risk since there is a contract
FCT-088.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC.
Analysis: A contract is necessary but insufficient; without evidence of services and benefit, the fee is disallowed (FCT-076). Contractor tax on payment still arises – a double cost.
Distractors: B and C are wrong in substance; D underestimates the risk.

FCT-089.q: Payments to a foreign supplier for goods delivered abroad (the buyer imports itself, with no services in Vietnam) are not subject to FCT.
FCT-089.e: True. Pure supply of goods without services in Vietnam is outside FCT.
FCT-089.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Buying goods delivered abroad, imported by the buyer, with no services in Vietnam is a pure goods supply – outside contractor tax. Taxes arise at import (import duty, import VAT).

FCT-090.q: Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, interest disallowed by the 30% EBITDA cap may be carried forward for at most:
FCT-090.e: Disallowed interest is carried forward for no more than 5 consecutive years.
FCT-090.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Disallowed interest is carried forward for up to 5 consecutive years (FCT-027).
Distractors: 3 years, 10 years and no carry-forward are wrong.

FCT-091.e: Vietnam applies the QDMTT and IIR; the UTPR is not yet applied under Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
o: TP documentation comprises the Local file, Master file and CbCR (if required).
The CbCR threshold for a Vietnamese ultimate parent is VND 18,000 billion.
Vietnam has applied the UTPR since 2024.
FCT-091.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
Analysis: (1) True – three-tier documentation. (2) True – the CbCR threshold is 18,000 billion VND. (3) False – Vietnam applies QDMTT and IIR; UTPR isn't applied. (4) True – 15% minimum rate.

FCT-092.q: A company hires a foreign company to train staff in Vietnam online at a gross (tax-inclusive) price of VND 210 million; VAT 5%; CIT 5%. How much is actually paid to the contractor after withholding (VND million)?
FCT-092.x:
Basis: Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: VAT = 210 × 5% = 10.5; CIT = (210 − 10.5) × 5% = 9.975; net payment = 210 − 10.5 − 9.975 = 189.525 million VND.
Note: Online training consumed in Vietnam is within contractor tax (FCT-002).

FCT-093.q: Decree 20/2025/ND-CP amends the rules so that interest on Government loans, concessional loans and loans for national target programmes is excluded when applying the 30% EBITDA cap.
FCT-093.e: True. Decree 20/2025/ND-CP clarifies and expands the interest items excluded from the cap.
FCT-093.x:
Basis: Decree 20/2025/ND-CP amending Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Decree 20/2025 widens the interest excluded from the 30% EBITDA cap: Government loans (ODA), concessional loans, national target programme and social housing loans… – avoiding constraints on policy projects.

FCT-094.q: Select ALL concepts that belong to the GloBE rules:
FCT-094.e: The 30% EBITDA cap belongs to the transfer pricing rules (Decree 132/2020/ND-CP), not GloBE.
FCT-094.x:
Basis: Resolution 107/2023/QH15; Decree 236/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: GloBE concepts: (A) GloBE income; (B) covered taxes; (C) SBIE.
Distractors: (D) The 30% EBITDA interest cap belongs to Decree 132/2020's TP rules, not GloBE.

FCT-095.q: Under Official Letter 7634/CT-QLNT (14/10/2026), international transport support services performed abroad and not consumed in Vietnam are outside the VAT Law.
FCT-095.e: True. However, the business must still issue invoices to the buyer under Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
FCT-095.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7634/CT-QLNT of 14/10/2026; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. International transport support services (handling, customs, packing…) performed and consumed abroad fall outside the VAT Law (VAT-107); the invoicing duty still applies.
